name: Quercetin
short: Human studies report rare, mild side effects; long-term high-dose safety is unknown. May alter levels of some drugs (CYP2C9, CYP2E1 and P-glycoprotein substrates).
text: A safety review found that adverse effects of supplemental quercetin in human studies were rarely reported and mild, but adequate data on long-term use (over 12 weeks) of high doses are not available. Animal studies raised possible concerns about worsening kidney damage in an already damaged kidney and promoting oestrogen-dependent cancers (animal data). Quercetin can alter the bioavailability of certain drugs; a systematic review found clinically significant interactions demonstrated for only a limited number of drugs, mainly involving CYP2C9, CYP2E1 and P-glycoprotein, with many predicted interactions not confirmed in humans.
